parsed.attack: The why_not_obvious is factually wrong, and that is what kills this. Huckleberry, Nara Baby and Baby Daybook already give a second caregiver a free writing seat on one household record, and Huckleberry already ships Live Activities for a running sleep and feed timer, so 'a second writing seat the incumbent won't ship because it cuts per-account revenue' describes the category leader's free tier. The remaining delta, either parent ending the running timer from their own lock screen, is one sprint for a team that already has the account model, the sync and the widget, and Apple is the second front the moment Health's family sharing covers infant feeding.
parsed.strongest_defence: Incumbent multi-caregiver support is asynchronous cloud sync with a mostly read-only partner view; a single live timer that either parent can end in place at four in the morning without unlocking and opening an app is a different interaction, and the overlapping-entry merge conflicts in kill criterion two are real evidence the incumbents have not solved concurrent writing, only concurrent viewing.
parsed.verdict_reason: The differentiator this idea claims nobody in the category ships is already free in the category leader's app, leaving a subscription with nothing distinctive to charge for.
